title: Fix Map direct launch from default launch-view
observed_behavior: When this uploaded fixture is launched with default view set to Map, the app can leave the Processing Files dialog visible indefinitely instead of finishing the launch. The failure was observed while Map was requesting zipcodes.csv and never reached the maintained assertions.
intended_behavior: The Processing Files dialog should clear and the uploaded network should reach an interactive Map view on the direct-launch path.
cause_summary: Map did not publish `networkRendered = true` after its first Leaflet draw cycle, so a direct launch that started in Map had no view-specific signal to release the shared Processing Files modal. The stable 2D-then-Map path masked that gap because 2D already emitted the render-complete signal.
fix_summary: Map now marks itself rendered after the first `onDataChange()` draw cycle completes, and maintained coverage now includes a dedicated uploaded direct-launch Map smoke that waits for Processing Files to clear before asserting zipcode-mapped rendering.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after the maintained uploaded direct-launch Map smoke passed locally in headless Chrome and confirmed the Processing Files modal clears on the true File Settings default-view = Map path.

title: Render Map links using uploaded style color mapping
observed_behavior: A historical Map-style probe compared rendered sports-team links against a stale hardcoded color expectation instead of the applied style-table mapping, which made the uploaded style-file path look broken even though the rendered Leaflet link colors already matched the applied Contact type table.
intended_behavior: Applying a style file on uploaded Map data should propagate both node and link color mappings into the rendered Leaflet layers and keep those rendered link colors aligned with the applied style-table state.
cause_summary: Not a product bug. On the uploaded style-file fixture, rendered Map sports-team, classroom, and family-member links already matched the applied `linkColorsTable['Contact type']` mapping; the old blocker came from a legacy hardcoded expectation rather than a propagation failure.
fix_summary: Restored maintained style-file coverage by asserting rendered Map link colors against the applied style-table mapping instead of the stale hardcoded color assumption.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after the maintained uploaded Map style-file journey passed locally with rendered link colors matching the applied Contact type style table.

title: Keep Map timeline slider node counts in sync
observed_behavior: An earlier uploaded-data probe treated any truthy `Zip_code` value as a renderable Map node during manual timeline slider clicks, which produced a persistent three-node mismatch between commonService visibility and the rendered Map featureGroup on the midpoint and start checkpoints.
intended_behavior: Manual timeline slider movement on Map should keep the rendered Leaflet node membership synchronized with the timeline-visible nodes that actually have map coordinates, just like the direct timeline-update oracle path does.
cause_summary: Not a product bug. The mismatch came from the maintained probe counting the fixture's P1/P2/P3 place rows as zipcode-backed nodes even though they stay timeline-visible without `_jlat`/`_jlon` and therefore are never renderable Map nodes.
fix_summary: Restored maintained manual-slider coverage by asserting oracle-backed rendered Map membership and by comparing rendered node ids against the visible nodes that actually have map coordinates instead of a naive truthy `Zip_code` count.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after the maintained uploaded Map timeline-controls journey passed locally with midpoint and start slider clicks aligned to the oracle-backed rendered node set.

title: Sync Map layer UI and widget state after settings load
observed_behavior: On uploaded zipcode-mapped Map data, the Map settings dialog could open before the component finished syncing its initial layer state, leaving the select-button UI at constructor defaults while the backing widgets still reflected the saved layer settings. The old load path also forced fallback layer selections during `loadSettings()` instead of restoring the saved widget state.
intended_behavior: Changing Map layer controls in the Components panel should keep the select-button UI, session widgets, and Leaflet layer presence synchronized for basemap and offline layers.
cause_summary: Map initialization used a blind `600ms` timeout after `onMapReady()`, so the settings UI could be inspected before the first real layer sync completed. Separately, `loadSettings()` rewrote the saved layer selections instead of replaying them directly.
fix_summary: Initial layer settings now wait for both the Leaflet map and marker-cluster group to be ready before the first sync runs, and `loadSettings()` now restores the saved basemap/satellite/countries/states/counties widget state instead of forcing fallback selections. Maintained uploaded-data coverage now exercises basemap hide plus countries/states/counties toggles end to end.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after the maintained uploaded Map layers journey passed locally with synchronized widget state and Leaflet layer presence for the basemap and offline toggle paths.

title: Keep uploaded Map link color mode as configured
observed_behavior: The uploaded zipcode-mapped COVID fixture originally forced the global link color-by path back to origin during UI-settings load, which blocked the maintained fixed-link and cluster-link Map journeys.
intended_behavior: The uploaded Map link color-by selector should preserve a valid None or Cluster selection so fixed link colors and cluster-driven link recoloring can be applied and verified on Map.
cause_summary: `loadUISettings()` was rewriting `link-color-variable = None` back to `origin`, so the uploaded Map fixed-link and cluster-color paths could not stay on the requested link-color mode.
fix_summary: Stopped forcing uploaded Map link-color state from `None` back to `origin`, then restored maintained fixed-link and threshold-driven cluster-recompute coverage. The later cluster-table failure was narrowed to an async Cypress timing issue and fixed by waiting for populated link-table rows before extraction.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after both maintained uploaded Map regressions passed locally: the fixed-link path now stays on `None`, and the cluster-recompute path was a table-population timing issue in the spec rather than a remaining product bug.

title: Allow Map link color edits while timeline mode is active
observed_behavior: A historical blocker assumed the uploaded Map timeline path needed an editable link color-table row, but the current fixture keeps `link-color-variable = None` during timeline mode and exposes the fixed `link-color` input instead.
intended_behavior: While Map timeline mode is active on uploaded data, both node and link colors should remain editable so color changes can be made during timeline mode and verified after Timeline is set back to None.
cause_summary: Not a product bug. On the maintained uploaded timeline path, link colors remain editable through the fixed `link-color` input even though no link color table is shown, and the rendered link color persists after timeline teardown.
fix_summary: Restored maintained node+link timeline-teardown coverage by combining the existing cluster-driven node color-table edit with a fixed link-color edit during timeline mode, then asserting both persist after `Timeline -> None`.
notes: Closed on 2026-04-08 after the maintained uploaded Map timeline color-persistence journey passed locally with both node and link colors surviving timeline teardown.
